newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Poor bidders seen delay to Russia Tyumen oil sale.
newsitem.headline: Poor bidders seen delay to Russia Tyumen oil sale.

text.p: A shortage of funds among Russian investors could be behind the postponement of a tender for a stake in Tyumen oil company (TNK), the chairman of the regional property fund said on Wednesday.

Vladimir Zagvyazinsky said he was sure the sale would take place before the end of 1997, though the size of the proposed stake could be reduced to allow a transfer of shares to the regional authority.
"The task of fulfilling the budget requires that the auction be carried out before the end of the financial year and I am certain that it will be," Zagvyazinsky said.

Russia has planned a number of sell-offs to help fill gaping government coffers. The stake in TNK, the main production unit of which is Nizhnevartovskneftegaz, is the largest among six energy company auctions recently announced.
TNK produced 21.3 million tonnes (426,000 barrels per day) of crude last year.

But the Russian Federal Property Fund and the Federal Securities Corporation, which are responsible for the TNK sale, announced last Friday that the tender due to take place from August 5 to September 26, would be postponed.
Zagvyazinsky said another TNK share sale and recent tenders for stakes in telecoms holding company Svyazinvest and Norilsk Nickel metals group appeared to have sucked up investment funds.

"Although there has been no official explanation for why the auction was put off, presumably the potential investors do not have enough money after the tenders for Svyazinvest, TNK and Norilsk Nickel to support the price level," Zagvyazinsky said.
Under the terms of the auction, companies intending to bid in the tender would have had to make a $755 million deposit before August 25.
Zagvyazinsky said it was also possible the stake offered would be less than the originally proposed 48.64 percent.
The regional administration wants the federal government to pay some of its debts with part of the federal stake, he said.
He said the Ministry of Finance owed Tyumen region 200 billion roubles ($34.5 million). "The region is planning to acquire TNK shares on this money," Zagvyazinsky said.
He added that Tyumen hoped to acquire around five to seven percent of shares at a discounted price. --Yelena Smirnova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520 ($ = 5805 Russian Roubles)
